scope: Theorem 3.5 (Local transference) of the manuscript “Weighted dilation graphs, smooth shifted primes and totient fibers” (preprints/Weighted-Dilation-Graphs-Smooth-Shifted-Primes-and-Totient-Fibers-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 011 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 351692885d112277), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 12. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every fixed E > 0 there is Eid > 0, depending only on E and the fixed data in Theorem 3.1, with the following property. Assume sup Θ∈R ∥T (Θ)∥ ≤ L−Eid . (3.6) Then, for every sufficiently large fixed J, where the lower bound on J may also depend on m, C1, put R = ⌈L0.52 ⌉, N = 2R. For every fixed γ > 0 and I = [X, 2X) with xγ ≤ X ≤ x1/γ, one has 1 |I ∩ Z| X n∈I∩Z ⟨un, (AA∗ )R un⟩ ≤ L−EN , (3.7) for all sufficiently large x. Here un is one on every physical state at position n and zero elsewhere. The threshold for x may depend on all fixed parameters, including J, C2, γ, and the bound is uniform subject to these parameters and Equation (3.6). No bound on ζ is needed apart from the assumed ideal estimate.
